reviews.body: The temperature guard at line 95 of anthropic.py admits the `anthropic.NOT_GIVEN` sentinel because it is falsy but not None, causing the sentinel string to appear in span metadata rather than the field being absent; the fix must restrict the check to numeric types to preserve zero while excluding omission sentinels. review_comments.body:
**![P2](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-F5C518?style=flat) Preserve omission of Anthropic’s unset temperature sentinel** When a caller explicitly forwards temperature=anthropic.NOT_GIVEN, the SDK treats the parameter as omitted. This non-None check now includes that falsy sentinel in metadata, and sanitization serializes it as "NOT_GIVEN". Previously the field was omitted. Filter out the sentinel while preserving numeric zero so span metadata reflects the request. ```suggestion if isinstance(kwargs.get("temperature"), (int, float)): ``` React: 👍 useful · 👎 wrong · 😕 unclear · 👀 right, but not acting on it

Good catch, thanks. The None check let `anthropic.NOT_GIVEN` through (falsy, not None), so it would have been recorded as `"NOT_GIVEN"`. Fixed in the new commit: `temperature` is recorded only when it is a number (`isinstance(..., (int, float))`), so `0` and `0.0` are kept and the sentinel is skipped. The test gains a falsy-sentinel case that fails with the previous check. Run in an environment without the Anthropic SDK, using a stand-in with the same truthiness.
